articles.title: ASI Hits $3 Billion Valuation in $325 Million Round Led by Spark
articles.summary: Startup ASI raised $325 million in new funding from investors, allowing the company to expand an artificial intelligence system that helps the military, airlines and air-traffic controllers manage assets.
articles.author: Ed Ludlow and Rebecca Torrence

articles.title: Tenstorrent CEO on New Funding Round, AI Progress
articles.summary: Tenstorrent CEO Jim Keller discussed the chip startup’s $1.5 billion funding round, which values the company at about $6.2 billion. He said the company is focused on scaling its Galaxy server program and developing AI intellectual property, rather than pursuing a sale. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Bailey Lipschultz on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: JPMorgan's 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions
articles.summary: David Kelly, chief global strategist at JPMorgan Asset Management, and Stephen Parker, co-head of global investment strategy at JPMorgan Private Bank, discuss their latest Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions report, which projects about 7% annual returns for 60/40 portfolios over the next 10–15 years. They speak on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Goldman's Lynam Isn't Worried About Access to Debt Amid AI Buildout
articles.summary: Amanda Lynam, chief credit strategist at Goldman Sachs, says recent widening in AI-related credit spreads resembles an earlier episode but differs because high-yield debt is now leading the move and investors are raising fundamental questions. She speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: AI Firm Nscale Faces Investor Pushback Over IPO Valuation
articles.summary: Bloomberg's Brody Ford said that issues facing the IPO of AI firm Nscale are 'endemic' to the larger AI data center industry as developers try to source power and labor and contend with potential delays. Bloomberg's Bailey Lipschultz said that the tone has shifted for AI IPOs as more companies slow down on going public before the end of the year. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Nscale’s $30B IPO Ambition Meets Investor Pushback
articles.summary: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow looks at why Nscale is facing pushback to its $30 billion IPO valuation target, with some investors suggesting $16 to $19 billion instead. Plus, Anthropic plans to put 5% of its shares into a new public benefit fund to address "the public good," and a former OpenAI software engineer charged with placing a recording device in one of the company's offices is set to appear in court today. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: The neocloud shakeout is coming, and Nvidia has the most to lose
articles.summary: After stock crashes and Firmus's scrapped IPO, industry executives expect only seven to ten of the hundreds of AI cloud providers to survive. CoreWeave lost a quarter of its market value, and Microsoft pulled out of a deal with Nscale for 23,000 Nvidia chips. Nvidia has a lot riding on the outcome, since customers outside the hyperscalers make up 45 percent of its data center revenue. The article The neocloud shakeout is coming, and Nvidia has the most to lose appeared first on The Decoder.
articles.author: Maximilian Schreiner

articles.title: Anthropic plans fund for workers threatened by AI, Musk counters with SpaceX shares for children
articles.summary: Anthropic wants to put five percent of its shares into a new public benefit fund that will also look into direct payments to workers at risk of losing their jobs. The fund is a company-owned LLC, so Anthropic keeps control of it as a possible IPO approaches. By offering the option of direct payments, Anthropic goes further than its competitors. Elon Musk says on X the company should just give the shares directly to the public. The article Anthropic plans fund for workers threatened by AI, Musk counters with SpaceX shares for children appeared first on The Decoder.
articles.author: Maximilian Schreiner

articles.title: Markets Brace for Inflation, Tech Earnings
articles.summary: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Inflation fears rattle markets as Meta leads a massive earnings week. Nvidia-backed Nscale faces a valuation reality check, while Trump-Zelenskyy tensions deepen. Plus, Proofpoint’s $6.3 billion Varonis deal; we talk with Thoma Bravo’s Seth Boro. And JPMorgan’s $230 billion economic-security push with Herman Chan, plus Ed Ludlow on Anthropic’s public-good pledge. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Musk pledges to give ‘every kid in America’ one of his SpaceX shares
articles.summary: Musk's post came just a few hours after Anthropic promised to put 5% of its shares into a new "public benefit fund," which it intends to use to make "large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations" after its upcoming IPO.
articles.author: Sean O'Kane

articles.title: Chip Startup Tenstorrent Raises Funds at $6.2 Billion Value
articles.summary: AI chip startup Tenstorrent Inc., after attracting takeover interest earlier this year, has raised $1.5 billion from investors in a funding round that boosts its valuation to $6.2 billion.
articles.author: Liana Baker and Ian King

articles.title: Korea Data Center IPO to Test AI Investor Resolve After Tumult
articles.summary: Data-center infrastructure company Elice Inc. is poised to debut on South Korea’s tech-heavy Kosdaq market Tuesday, testing AI investors’ nerves after peer Firmus canceled its high-profile listing this month.
articles.author: Yoolim Lee

articles.title: AuxoAI raises over $20M to bring AI expertise to the enterprise and redesign how work gets done
articles.summary: AuxoAI Inc., an enterprise engineering and consulting company that helps large businesses build and deploy artificial intelligence systems, today announced it has raised $20.7 million in a Series A funding to accelerate growth and scale its enterprise AI consulting model. The company said it has spent over three years working with Global 2000 enterprises and […] The post AuxoAI raises over $20M to bring AI expertise to the enterprise and redesign how work gets done appeared first on SiliconANGLE.
articles.author: Kyt Dotson

articles.title: I’m a CTO. AI still needs your human expertise | Madhu Shashanka
articles.summary: AI is increasingly getting good at doing some tasks, but it can never replace human workers’ judgmentAutonomous cars, which may be the safest we have built, keep getting easily avoidable parking tickets. While Waymos crash far less often than human drivers over tens of millions of miles, they’re still terrible at performing basic tasks – keeping out of disabled parking spots and tow-away zones, or steering clear of a church garage during Sunday service, according to the Wall Street Journal.That is the state of AI today: impressively capable at something complex, yet embarrassingly clumsy at something easy. And it has implications for what work will remain human and what will be automated by AI.Madhu Shashanka is co-founder, chief scientist and chief technology officer at Concentric AI, a data security software company Continue reading...
articles.author: Madhu Shashanka

articles.title: How To Build A Billion-Dollar Company Without Venture Capital
articles.summary: Founders can build billion-dollar businesses without venture capital by prioritizing customer revenue, pricing for quality, hiring exceptional talent and automating processes to scale efficiently, argues Nacho De Marco, who draws on his experience bootstrapping BairesDev, to emphasize financial discipline and a lasting commitment to solving customer problems as the foundations of sustainable growth.
articles.author: Guest Author

articles.title: JP Morgan Strategist on AI Jitters, Investing Outlook
articles.summary: Jordan Jackson, JPMorgan Asset Management Global Market Strategist, discusses whether earnings growth may be nearing a peak even if results are not worsening. Jackson agrees that third-quarter results are expected to be strong, with forecasts calling for about 27% to 28% year-over-year earnings growth. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Kristine Aquino on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Financing The AI Boom: Masters in Business with Bob Michele
articles.summary: Barry speaks with Bob Michele, CIO and Head of Global Fixed Income, Currency, and Commodities at JPMorgan. They discuss Bob's unconventional start at the University of Pennsylvania, the differences between the science of bonds and the art of equities, and whether the US is heading toward a recession. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: SoftBank Is Said to Weigh Buying Top US Security Firm Allied
articles.summary: SoftBank Group Corp. is considering an acquisition of Allied Universal, the largest security services company in the US, people familiar with the matter said, as founder Masayoshi Son explores ways to deploy AI-powered robots across industries.
articles.author: Carmen Arroyo, Min Jeong Lee, Manuel Baigorri and Paula Sambo

articles.title: CoreWeave, Nscale Put Neocloud Economics in Focus
articles.summary: Concerns about the enormous amounts of debt financing the AI infrastructure boom are putting the neocloud sector under increasing scrutiny. Decoding Discontinuity CEO Raphaelle D’Ornano discusses the pressure on CoreWeave as interest expenses weigh on its economics. She explains why investors are looking beyond contracted backlogs to financed and energized capacity, and how Nscale’s vertically integrated approach differs as it prepares for a potential IPO. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Nscale's Flagship Data Center Hit by Delays Ahead of IPO
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence infrastructure firm Nscale is seeking to raise up to $3 billion in an initial public offering as soon as this month, just as investors are growing increasingly wary of the risks of the AI buildout. The UK firm has also been hit by regulatory hurdles, a fire and other delays during construction of a flagship data center in Norway. Bloomberg's Paula Doenecke reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
